page: Microsoft Azure DC4ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration backed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The system features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processor, utilizing simultaneous multithreading with 2 threads per core. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory is sized at 16.0 GB RAM, adhering to a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). The instance is bundled with 161 GB of local SSD storage and does not include dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results reflect the entry-level core density of the configuration. Single-threaded testing demonstrates typical performance for its hardware generation, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2185.16 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1219.0 falling into average ranges. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics place in the bottom 25%, as seen in the Geekbench multi-core score of 2686.0 and PassMark CPU score of 4724.98. Hardware-accelerated instruction support includes AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, which maintains mid-tier encryption throughput in PassMark testing (2896.33), whereas AVX-512 extensions are absent.

Data operations and memory-bound metrics align with smaller general-purpose VM tiers. PassMark memory testing scored 1701.64, while database operations reached 1441.89 and Redis recorded 3.06 million SET operations per second, both registering in the lower quartile of overall cloud benchmarks. The included 161 GB local SSD provides fast scratch space, but the 2 physical cores limit sustained parallel execution.

The DC4ads_v5 offers balanced cost efficiency for lightweight server roles that require consistent dedicated CPU resources without massive core parallelism. It is appropriate for general-purpose workloads, standard web serving, small databases, development and CI environments, and caching layers with modest throughput requirements.
description: Microsoft Azure DC4ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor on the x86_64 architecture. Sized with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 16.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio alongside 161 GB of integrated local SSD storage. Benchmark evaluations show moderate single-core performance, achieving 1219.0 in Geekbench single-core, but parallel workloads are constrained by the two-core physical topology, leading to bottom-quartile results in multi-core metrics like PassMark CPU (4724.98) and Redis SET operations (3.06 million ops/sec). The CPU includes hardware crypto extensions such as AES and SHA-NI while omitting AVX-512. The instance is suited for general application hosting, small database nodes, and lightweight web serving workloads.
